items.title: Why Pluto was reclassified
items.claim: The IAU's 2006 definition of 'planet' has three conditions: it orbits the Sun, has enough mass for hydrostatic equilibrium, and what?
items.reveal_title: 'Cleared the neighbourhood' is the criterion Pluto fails
items.reveal:
Pluto orbits within the Kuiper Belt with comparable bodies (notably Eris). The IAU created the 'dwarf planet' category.

Ceres in the asteroid belt is also a dwarf planet under the definition.
items.why: Scientific categories sometimes change to track the evidence rather than vice versa.

items.title: How the CMB was found
items.claim: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson discovered the cosmic microwave background in 1964 while working at Bell Labs. What were they originally trying to do?

options.text: Refining a horn antenna for radio communications, with the persistent noise traced to a cosmic source

items.reveal_title: An accidental discovery in a communications lab
items.reveal:
Penzias and Wilson were eliminating noise sources, including pigeon droppings inside the antenna. The Princeton group nearby was independently looking for exactly this signal.

Nobel Prize 1978 went to Penzias and Wilson.
items.why: Major cosmological evidence has come from accident as often as from targeted experiment.

items.title: The first confirmed exoplanets
items.claim: The first exoplanets confirmed orbited an unusual host. What was it?

options.text: A pulsar (PSR B1257+12), with the discovery announced in 1992

items.reveal_title: Pulsar planets, three years before 51 Pegasi b
items.reveal:
Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail confirmed planets around the millisecond pulsar PSR B1257+12 in 1992.

Mayor and Queloz's 51 Pegasi b (1995) was the first around a sunlike star and won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
items.why: Public memory often centres on the second discovery if the first occurs in an exotic setting.
